text:
rahul: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a `deferredRetry` option on paginated iterators. Idea: SDK schedules retries for transient failures on *future* pages in the background instead of blocking the caller. Less head-of-line blocking for sync users, and nicer UX for streaming reads. :thinking:

cam: Sounds promising. Can you sketch the exact surface? I worry about memory blow-ups if we prefetch & retry too eagerly.

rahul: Agreed, the surface should be conservative. Sketch: default off. When enabled, SDK will: 1) fetch page N synchronously, return it; 2) if fetch for N+1 fails transiently, schedule a retry worker with bounded queue and backoff; 3) expose `iterator.prefetch(depth=1|2)` and `iterator.deferredRetryPolicy(name)` for advanced users. Example (TS):

```ts
const it = client.listItems({pageSize: 100, deferredRetry: true});
for await (const page of it.pages()) {
  // page processing unaffected by transient N+1 failures
}

// advanced:
it.prefetch(2);
it.deferredRetryPolicy({maxAttempts: 5, backoffMs: 200});
```

tina: How do we model cancellation? If caller cancels iteration, we should stop background retries ASAP and drop queued work. Also need to surface telemetry: queuedRetries, activeRetries, lastRetryError.

eli: Language constraints: python's sync iterators can't do background threads without giving the user weird semantics. In Python we'd use a background ThreadPoolExecutor limited to 1 worker per iterator and prefer the async iterator for more concurrency. TS/node: use internal async tasks + setImmediate. Go: spin a goroutine per iterator but bound with token bucket.

sasha: What about idempotency? If pages are not idempotent (server side cursor advances) background retries could cause duplicate side effects on read+ack flows. We should only enable deferredRetry for idempotent read-only paged endpoints or when server advertises 'safeToRetry=true' via response metadata.

cam: We already have server metadata bits in some responses. Add `retryHint: { safeToRetry: bool, suggestedBackoffMs: number }`. SDKs should respect that by default.

rahul: Implementation concerns: 1) bounded memory: prefetch queue size = depth * pageSize").slice(0,1) + "", // keep message short

eli: Also think about ordering guarantees. If background retry returns a page later than a newer page, we must ensure iterator.pages() yields in correct order. So background work should only ever attempt missing next page(s); it should not race ahead and push later pages early.

rahul: Good point — algorithm: always fetch next sequential page (N+1) only after N has been returned. Background retries only try to complete the immediate next gap(s). No parallel outrunning.

sasha: Failure semantics: if retries exhaust, iterator should surface a terminal error on next access (or optional fallback to a compatible model/route). We should expose `onDeferredRetryExhausted` hook so product teams can wire fallbacks.

cam: Tests: need unit tests for cancellation + resource cleanup, stress tests for many iterators in parallel, and e2e with flaky network to assert latency SLOs don't regress.

tina: Telemetry + cost: track retry token consumption, additional RPCs, and surface as optional debug trace. Add a console flag `DEFERRED_RETRY_VERBOSE` for local debugging.

rahul: Backwards compatibility: keep iterator semantics identical when disabled. For enabled mode, document strong invariants: no duplicate pages, no ordering changes, best-effort completion for transient errors.

eli: API nit for Python: maybe `client.list_items(..., deferred_retry=True)` and return an object with `.pages()` and `.close()` to cancel background work.

sasha: Go sample API:
```go
it := client.ListItems(ctx, opts.WithDeferredRetry(true))
defer it.Close()
for it.Next() {
  page := it.Page()
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { /* handle */ }
```

rahul: Security: ensure retries don't re-send sensitive ephemeral tokens; if adapter needs to refresh creds, tie into auth refresh flows.

cam: Sounds actionable. Can you draft a short RFC appendix with: API sketches per-language, bounded resource semantics, telemetry keys, and a minimal server `retryHint` spec? If folks are happy we'll slot a follow-up design doc and a small spike for python & ts.

rahul: Will do. @sasha @eli @tina — want to co-author the appendix?

sasha: Happy to.

eli: I'll take the python bits + tests.

tina: I'll own telemetry and perf tests.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: add feature-flag, integration-tests, perf-suite.

cam: Great, thx everyone. Filing a short appendix tomorrow. :shipit:
